wake-up.title: Financial readiness quiz
wake-up.subtitle: Ten quick questions to see where you stand — with concrete next steps for every weak spot.

intro.title: Answer honestly — nothing leaves this device
intro.description: Score up to {max} points. You'll get your readiness level and action tips once all questions are answered.

q1.label: Do you have an emergency fund?

options.a: Yes — six or more months of expenses
options.c: Started one, but under three months

q1.tip: Build an emergency fund covering 3–6 months of essential expenses. It protects every other financial goal from surprise setbacks.

q2.label: How do you plan your monthly spending?

options.a: Written budget that I follow each month
options.b: A rough plan in my head

q2.tip: Give every baht/dollar a job before the month starts. A simple written budget is the fastest way to find leaky spending.

q3.label: Do you track where your money goes?
q3.tip: Track spending for one full month (an app or notebook both work). You can't optimize what you never measure.

q4.label: How much of your income do you save?
q4.tip: Pick a fixed savings rate you can sustain — even 5–10% — and raise it by 1% every few months. Pay yourself first.

q5.label: How are you handling debt?
q5.tip: List debts by balance and rate, then target extra payments at one debt (smallest balance or highest rate). Minimums keep you in debt longest.

q6.label: Are you saving for retirement?
q6.tip: Start now even if the amount feels small — time in the market compounds. Increase contributions with every raise.

q7.label: Do you know what your insurance covers?
q7.tip: Review health, life, and disability coverage annually. Gaps discovered after a claim are expensive lessons.

q8.label: Do your goals have amounts and dates?
q8.tip: Turn wishes into targets: give each goal an amount, a date, and a monthly contribution. Then track progress visibly.

q9.label: Are savings and bills automated?
q9.tip: Automate the important moves: savings on payday, bills on due dates. Willpower is a terrible long-term strategy.

q10.label: When did you last check your credit health?
q10.tip: Check your credit report and score at least yearly. Errors are common and fixing them early keeps borrowing cheap.
